subject: health
topic: Light at night is linked to weight and health
angle: Exposure to light at night is linked to increased obesity and various mental health conditions, though its specific link to depression is not statistically significant in all analyses.
title: The cost of light at night

reveal.headline: Light at night is linked to a 14% increased risk of obesity.
reveal.body: Exposure to light during the night is associated with higher body weight in the highest exposure groups.

explain.headline: Light exposure affects your metabolism and mental health.
explain.body: Research links light at night to increased risks of obesity and depression. While evidence for depression is inconsistent, the link to metabolic issues is established.

matters.headline: Your environment shapes your physical health.
matters.body: The lights in your home may be influencing your weight and mental state. That may be why your body feels different at night.

question.headline: What are you letting into your room at night?

stat.label: increased risk of obesity in the highest light exposure group

claims.text: Exposure to light at night is linked to a 14% increased risk of obesity in the highest exposure group compared to the lowest.
claims.quote: A significant 14% increased risk of obesity was observed in the highest LAN exposure group compared to the lowest (OR = 1. 14, 95% CI: 1. 07-1. 22; I² = 92. 5%, P 0. 05).

claims.text: Blue-enriched white light with a color temperature greater than 5000 Kelvin improves sleepiness in night-shift workers.
claims.quote: Further, the blue-enriched white light with a color temperature greater than 5000 Kelvin was effective in improving sleepiness of night-shift workers.

claims.text: Light at night is linked to an increased risk of depression.
claims.quote: Our findings suggest that both outdoor and indoor ALAN exposures are associated with increased risk of depression.

claims.text: Sleep interventions, including light therapy, improve sleep or reduce sleep disturbance among rotating night shift workers.
claims.quote: Conclusion Sleep interventions were effective in promoting sleep or reducing sleep disturbance among rotating night shift workers.

verdict: The evidence shows that light at night is associated with metabolic issues like obesity and several mental health disorders, while specific lighting interventions can improve sleepiness in shift workers.
caveat: The evidence for depression is inconsistent, with one meta-analysis failing to reach statistical significance.
caption:
Light at night is linked to metabolic and mental health changes.

Meta-analyses show a link to increased obesity and depression, though the evidence for depression is inconsistent across different studies. Light interventions can improve sleepiness for shift workers.

How much light do you see before you sleep?
